narrative.title: The Ledger Roll-Up Verification
narrative.scenario: A finance bot keeps its books as a binary tree where each account node should hold exactly the total rolling up from everything beneath it — the node's own balance must equal the combined totals of its two sub-ledgers. Before the quarter closes, the auditor asks a single yes/no question: does every non-leaf balance reconcile with the roll-up beneath it?
narrative.inputFormat: A binary tree as a level-order array (null marks a missing child), given by its root.
narrative.outputFormat: Return true if every non-leaf node's value equals the sum of its left and right subtree totals; otherwise return false.

testCases.explanation: The root's 3 is exactly 1 + 2, and both children are leaves that need no check.
26 rolls up 20 (from the 10-4-6 wing) plus 6 (from the 3-3 wing); every internal node reconciles.

hintLevels: Level 1: Ask each node a two-part question — am I consistent, and how much do I and my descendants hold?
Level 2: A leaf reports just its own value; an internal node reports twice its value only when the roll-up matches exactly.
Level 3: A sentinel like an impossible value can carry the 'already broken' flag so one mismatch poisons every ancestor.
